previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for his first maintenance cycle of high-dose methotrexate following reinduction therapy for relapsed primary central nervous system lymphoma. He reported excellent functional status since his last admission, with no neurological deficits or systemic symptoms. The methotrexate infusion was administered on day one and well tolerated. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion and continued until methotrexate levels dropped to 0.05, at which point it was safely discontinued. Hypokalemia developed secondary to bicarbonate-induced alkalinization and was managed with IV and oral potassium supplementation. Transaminitis was observed but remained within expected limits. Constipation was prevented with senna, docusate, and magnesium citrate. GERD management included a temporary switch from omeprazole to ranitidine during treatment, with resumption of the PPI at discharge. Aspirin was held during hospitalization and restarted upon discharge due to family history of coronary artery disease. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to receive rituximab in clinic the following week and return for his next methotrexate infusion in one month.
